description: Baseline extracted shared temporal decision engine and added a scenario-suite benchmark for noisy hold detection accuracy.

asi.hypothesis: A realistic temporal benchmark around noisy sustained holds, dropouts, and spike rejection will expose whether gesture accuracy improvements are possible without touching model weights.
asi.learned: Current logic never false-triggers in the suite but misses many borderline holds because any brief misclassification fully resets the 3s timer.
asi.next_action_hint: Try temporal smoothing / grace-window logic that tolerates short gaps without allowing spike-based false triggers.

description: Added a short interruption grace window so sustained holds survive brief 'None' dropouts instead of restarting immediately.

asi.hypothesis: Real webcam streams often contain single-frame losses; tolerating very short interruptions should increase hold-trigger recall more than it harms false positives.
asi.learned: A 220ms dropout grace improved recall materially (+11 fewer misses) with only one new false trigger across the synthetic suite.
asi.tradeoff: Grace windows help on detection dropouts but can leak into false positives if they also forgive wrong-gesture intervals.
asi.next_action_hint: Differentiate between benign dropouts and explicit wrong gestures; keep forgiving 'None'/no-hand blips but be stricter when a different gesture is seen.

description: Tried asymmetric grace windows: longer forgiveness for no-hand dropouts and shorter forgiveness for visible-hand uncertain frames.

asi.hypothesis: Visible-hand 'None' classifications may be riskier than full tracking loss, so asymmetric grace might preserve recall while reducing false positives.
asi.rollback_reason: No measurable improvement versus the prior grace-window version; metrics were identical on the suite.
asi.learned: The lone false trigger is not caused by treating no-hand and visible-hand 'None' equally, or at least not at the tested thresholds.
asi.next_action_hint: Try structural smoothing of raw gesture labels before hold timing, such as short majority voting or score accumulation, rather than only tweaking reset thresholds.

description: Allowed very brief wrong-gesture blips before resetting an active hold, so single-frame misclassifications no longer destroy near-complete holds.

asi.hypothesis: MediaPipe can momentarily classify the wrong gesture even while the user's true pose is unchanged; a short confirmation window before switching gestures should recover many missed holds.
asi.learned: This was the big bottleneck: forgiving ~90ms of wrong-gesture noise collapsed misses from 97 to 10, but it also increased accidental triggers to 10 and slightly raised timing latency.
asi.tradeoff: Much higher recall at the cost of some false-positive risk; likely closer to real-world usability, but worth trying follow-up guardrails to trim the false triggers.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the switch-confirmation idea and explore lightweight anti-spike guardrails, such as requiring a minimum number of matching frames before trigger once recovery from interruption has occurred.

description: Aligned engine output with the stabilized active gesture so triggers fire for the debounced decision instead of the noisy instantaneous frame label.

asi.hypothesis: If smoothing decides a hold is valid, the emitted gesture should reflect that stabilized decision; otherwise the app can miss real triggers during brief noisy frames.
asi.learned: This fixed the remaining misses/false positives in the suite: the prior errors were largely output-alignment bugs, not the hold logic itself.
asi.bug_root_cause: `isTriggered` was derived from `activeGesture`, but `gesture` returned to the app remained the raw current frame, allowing `None` or a wrong one-frame blip to suppress or mislabel the action.
asi.next_action_hint: Probe for over-aggressive behavior with harder adversarial scenarios; if current logic holds up, document the change and capture future ideas rather than adding complexity for tiny gains.

name: Optimize EasyCord gesture recognition accuracy (expanded adversarial benchmark)
